Overview:

Sprout is a global IT hardware retirement provider for hyperscaler and enterprise clients. We leverage a nationwide footprint (and international partner network) combined with proprietary software to enable efficient end-to-end IT asset disposition with a focus on data-bearing devices from the client to the cloud. The company is headquartered in Charlotte, NC with additional operations near Sacramento, Dallas, and Boston. Sprout provides software and services to clients in the form of our IT Asset Disposition, Certified Destruction, and Responsible Recycling solutions.

Since our founding as an electronic waste startup from a Duke University dorm room in 2014, we have been expanding at an average rate of >50% each year. By adhering to our 3 values (One Sprout, Deliver Excellence, and Integrity Matters), we are proud of our culture to move at #SproutSpeed seeking to become the emerging leader in our industry

The Technical Project Manager owns datacenter hardware projects across the full asset lifecycle — from initial buildout and infrastructure configuration, through steady-state operations handover, to end-of-life decommissioning and disposition. This role is the single point of accountability that keeps complex, multi-vendor hardware programs on schedule, on budget, and on spec while coordinating engineering, facilities, supply chain, and vendor teams. It is a delivery-focused role for someone equally comfortable in a project plan and on a datacenter floor, and who can translate technical detail into clear stakeholder communication.

Responsibilities:

* Plan and manage datacenter buildout projects end to end — site readiness, rack and power layout, cabling, and network fabric — against defined milestones
* Coordinate facilities, engineering, and vendor teams to deliver hardware installation on schedule and to spec
* Manage scope, dependencies, and site logistics across concurrent buildout efforts
* Drive the build and configuration of compute, storage, and network infrastructure to specification
* Manage burn-in, validation, and acceptance testing before production release
* Ensure configurations, firmware, and standards are consistent and documented across deployments
* Lead the transition of newly deployed infrastructure into steady-state operations
* Ensure runbooks, monitoring, documentation, and support ownership are in place before handover
* Confirm operations readiness and sign-off with receiving teams
* Manage decommissioning of end-of-life hardware — safe power-down, de-racking, and removal
* Oversee data sanitization, asset tracking, and compliant resale, recycling, or destruction
* Maintain regulatory and chain-of-custody compliance throughout the disposition process
* Build and maintain integrated project schedules, budgets, risk registers, and status reporting across all lifecycle phases
* Coordinate vendors, contractors, and internal stakeholders, holding each accountable to scope, timeline, and quality
* Track hardware assets and maintain accurate lifecycle records in the CMDB / asset management system
* Identify risks and dependencies early, drive resolution, and escalate clearly when decisions or trade-offs are needed

Qualifications:

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Information Technology, Business Management, or related field (or equivalent experience)
* Several years of technical project management experience delivering datacenter or IT infrastructure hardware projects
* Demonstrated experience across the hardware lifecycle: datacenter buildout, infrastructure build and configuration, operations handover, and decommissioning and disposition
* Certifications are a plus — e.g., PMP, PRINCE2, or CSM for project management, and datacenter / infrastructure credentials such as CDCP/CDCS, ITIL, or relevant vendor certifications (Cisco, Dell, HPE)
* Experience with ITAD, data sanitization standards (e.g., NIST 800-88), and environmental / chain-of-custody compliance is a plus

Risk Adjustment Data Analyst
  
Position Summary
  
The Risk Adjustment Data Analyst supports end to end risk adjustment and revenue cycle operations by analyzing HCC submissions by ArchWell Health and any rejections at Clearninghouse/payer/CMS level, managing chart retrieval and review workflows, and ensuring accurate ingestion of care gap and clinical documentation data for various sources. This role is critical to maintaining RAF accuracy, reducing submission errors, and enabling continuous monthly reconciliation across MA programs. The role requires flexibility to perform additional tasks as needed, especially as risk adjustment and quality requirements evolve across markets and programs.
  
Key Responsibilities
  
HCC Reconciliation & Submission Validation
  

* Perform monthly validation of all HCC submissions (MAO004, encounters, claims, sweeps).
* Analyze payer acceptance, rejections, and 277CA/999 acknowledgement files.
* Identify new, recaptured, and dismissed HCCs and reconcile against internal systems (VIM, HCC engine).
* Present and route any rejections/gaps for appropriate teams.

Sweeps & Payer Data Management
  

* Review sweeps datasets to ensure completeness, accuracy, and payer acceptance.
* Support ASM workflows and monitor acceptance/rejection trends.
* Track payer healthcare gaps and validate alignment with internal care gap logic.

Chart Retrieval & Review Support
  

* Build and maintain chart retrieval/review prioritization rules (1LR, 2LR, external providers).
* Monitor chart retrieval programs, turnaround times, and vendor performance.
* ROI analysis of various programs
* Manage unlinked charts and ensure proper linkage to members, service dates, and HCCs.

Care Gap & Clinical Data Ingestion
  

* Support ingestion/analysis health plan care gap files and ensure accurate mapping into VIM and analyze suspects conversion rate from various sources.
* Validate care gap completeness and partner with clinical teams to ensure data is actionable.
* Develop or refine member stratification logic for outreach and in home visit prioritization.

Reporting & Analytics
  

* Build/Maintain dashboards and reports to track HCC operations work inclusive of reconciliation, chart retrieval progress, and rejection trends.
* Provide insights to leadership on productivity, throughput, and operational bottlenecks at market/center/payer level.

The Security Manager oversees the daily operations of the hospital security program to maintain a safe and secure environment for patients, visitors, staff and hospital property. This position supervises Access Control Personnel (ACP) and Agency Security Officers, coordinates daily security operations and implements security policies and procedures, workplace violence (WPV) prevention initiatives and emergency response protocols. The Security Manager develops and delivers security training for hospital staff and contract security personnel, leads security-related investigations, recommends corrective actions and collaborates with hospital leadership and law enforcement to resolve security concerns. This role also supports emergency preparedness, participates in Hospital Incident Command System (HICS) activations, and promotes continuous improvement through risk reduction, regulatory compliance and best security practices.

Responsibilities:

Plan, direct, supervise & evaluate the work of access control personnel (ACP) and agency security officers (ASO) to ensure effective security operations, regulatory compliance & exceptional customer service. Provide coaching, performance feedback and corrective action as needed while promoting accountability and professional standards.

Develop, implement and maintain hospital access control, visitor management and weapons screening programs in compliance with applicable regulatory and accreditation requirements. Serve as the security lead during incidents, coordinating response efforts with hospital leadership and law enforcement when appropriate.

Schedule, assign and coordinate staffing to ensure appropriate security coverage and operational readiness throughout the facility while fostering a collaborative, service-oriented culture focused on safety, professionalism and continuous improvement.

Design and deliver security training for ACPs, ASOs and hospital staff on site-specific security procedures, WPV prevention, de-escalation techniques, emergency code responses, incident reporting and customer service expectations.

Develop, implement and maintain the annual Security and WPV Prevention Training Program to meet organizational, regulatory and accreditation requirements. Evaluate program effectiveness through drills, exercises, after-action reviews and participating feedback.

Provide operational leadership during security incidents and emergencies. Serve as a member of hospital incident command (HICS) during activations and coordinate security operations with hospital leadership, emergency responders and law enforcement.

Lead multi-disciplanary reviews of security-related policies and procedures, including facility/Emergency Department lockdowns, patient elopement prevention and response, Code Grey, Code Pink/Purple, active shooter response, weapons screening response and other emergency security protocols. Conduct drills and after-action reviews to identify opportunities for improvement.

Investigate all security-related incidents, including workplace violence events, threats, assaults, thefts or other safety concerns. Analyze trends, identify contributing factors, recommend corrective actions and present findings to the Safety Committee and WPV Prevention Committee. Partner with leadership and law enforcement as needed to implement corrective actions, monitor outcomes and strengthen the hospitals safety and security programs.

Knowledge of healthcare security operations, access control, visitor management, weapons screening and emergency preparedness. Working knowledge of applicable hospital regulatory and hospital accreditation requirements, CMS, OSHA, EMTALA and state regulations governing healthcare security. Proficiency with security technologies, incident reporting systems and Microsoft Office applications.

Overview:

The Security Manager oversees the daily operations of the hospital security program to maintain a safe and secure environment for patients, visitors, staff and hospital property. This position supervises Access Control Personnel (ACP) and Agency Security Officers, coordinates daily security operations and implements security policies and procedures, workplace violence (WPV) prevention initiatives and emergency response protocols. The Security Manager develops and delivers security training for hospital staff and contract security personnel, leads security-related investigations, recommends corrective actions and collaborates with hospital leadership and law enforcement to resolve security concerns. This role also supports emergency preparedness, participates in Hospital Incident Command System (HICS) activations, and promotes continuous improvement through risk reduction, regulatory compliance and best security practices.

Responsibilities:

Plan, direct, supervise & evaluate the work of access control personnel (ACP) and agency security officers (ASO) to ensure effective security operations, regulatory compliance & exceptional customer service. Provide coaching, performance feedback and corrective action as needed while promoting accountability and professional standards.

Develop, implement and maintain hospital access control, visitor management and weapons screening programs in compliance with applicable regulatory and accreditation requirements. Serve as the security lead during incidents, coordinating response efforts with hospital leadership and law enforcement when appropriate.

Schedule, assign and coordinate staffing to ensure appropriate security coverage and operational readiness throughout the facility while fostering a collaborative, service-oriented culture focused on safety, professionalism and continuous improvement.

Design and deliver security training for ACPs, ASOs and hospital staff on site-specific security procedures, WPV prevention, de-escalation techniques, emergency code responses, incident reporting and customer service expectations.

Develop, implement and maintain the annual Security and WPV Prevention Training Program to meet organizational, regulatory and accreditation requirements. Conduct classroom instruction, hands-on defensive tactics, personal safety, Code Grey response and de-escalation training. Evaluate program effectiveness through drills, exercises, after-action reviews and participating feedback.

Provide operational leadership during security incidents and emergencies. Serve as a member of hospital incident command (HICS) during activations and coordinate security operations with hospital leadership, emergency responders and law enforcement.

Lead multi-disciplanary reviews of security-related policies and procedures, including facility/Emergency Department lockdowns, patient elopement prevention and response, Code Grey, Code Pink/Purple, active shooter response, weapons screening response and other emergency security protocols. Conduct drills and after-action reviews to identify opportunities for improvement.

Investigate all security-related incidents, including workplace violence events, threats, assaults, thefts or other safety concerns. Analyze trends, identify contributing factors, recommend corrective actions and present findings to the Safety Committee and WPV Prevention Committee. Partner with leadership and law enforcement as needed to implement corrective actions, monitor outcomes and strengthen the hospitals safety and security programs.

Research and evaluate environmental security controls to enhance the safety and security of patients, visitors, staff and hospital assets. Collaborate with stakeholders to deploy approved environmental security measures with best practice protocols.

Qualifications:

**Education:** Bachelor's degree in an appropriate discipline; OR, an equivalent combination of education, training and experience to provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties of the position.

**Experience:** Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in security, law enforcement, military, healthcare security, or a related public safety field as well as a minimum of two (2) years of supervisory or management experience leading security personnel. Experience in a healthcare environment, behavioral health setting, or other high-risk public environment preferred.

**Licenses & Certifications:** Valid California driver's license with no restrictions required. Crisis Prevention Institute (CPI), Management of Aggressive Behavior (MOAB), or equivalent de-escalation instructor certification preferred or required within one (1) year of hire. FEMA Incident Command System(ICS) 100, 200, 700 and 800 certifications required within one (1) year of hire. Instructor certification in defensive tactics, WPV prevention or related security training preferred.

**Required Skills & Knowledge:** Demonstrated leadership, supervisory and team development skills. Ability to remain calm, exercise strong judgement and make timely decisions during emergencies and high stress situations. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to build collaborative relationships across all organizational levels. Strong organizational and analytical skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced healthcare environment. Knowledge of healthcare security operations, access control, visitor management, weapons screening and emergency preparedness. Knowledge of WPV prevention programs, threat assessment, behavioral emergency response, trauma-informed security practices and de-escalation techniques. Working knowledge of applicable hospital regulatory and hospital accreditation requirements, CMS, OSHA, EMTALA and state regulations governing healthcare security. Proficiency with security technologies, incident reporting systems and Microsoft Office applications.

Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. The people here at Apple don’t just create products - they create the kind of wonder that’s revolutionized entire industries. It’s the diversity of those people and their ideas that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do, from amazing technology to industry-leading environmental efforts. Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it.  
  
In this highly visible role, you will have process (TPM) and quality engineering (MQE) responsibility for next generation Apple products. This will require you to lead selection, implementation & optimization of manufacturing processes and quality planning and deployment.  
  
In the TPM responsibility, you will utilize your Engineering experience and work cross functionally with Product Design Engineering and Industrial Design to assess product features for manufacturability, and recommend capable processes and equipment.  
  
In the MQE responsibility, you work in tandem with Apple's renowned designers to develop measurement & metrology technologies, quality control plans, information systems, and manufacturing methods that achieve industry-leading specifications at massive production scale. We handle a network of supplier factories worldwide, with responsibility for our partners to deliver to bold schedules. Our focus is on elegant execution of extraordinary industrial designs, resulting in products that thrill our customers.  
  
**Description**  
  
Process Development:  
  
Planning, proposing, and leading experiments to produce timely and accurate analyses used to drive design, development, and supply chain decisions.  
  
Assessing the suitability of a fabrication technology for a given part design. Planning validation exercises to demonstrate initial feasibility as well as manufacturing capability. Analyzing results of validation exercises and provide technical recommendations.  
  
Reviewing progress of development activities at supplier locations and serve as point of escalation for critical process related issues.  
  
New Product Introduction:  
  
Help to drive process development and capability assessment activities, reviewing part design documentation to ensure alignment with process capability.  
  
Assigns specific tasks and work with Apple suppliers to support process development and/or data gathering activities. Set clear goals for results and provide timely reviews of performance throughout program.  
  
Establish validation procedures to figure out acceptance of tooling into development builds as well as mass production.  
  
Supplier Execution:  
  
Review supplier tool design, process flow, equipment selection, DFM, and DOE proposals. Identify shortfalls and corrective actions to ensure design compliance.  
  
Work with supplier engineering teams to map out process development exercises, secure resources, and commit to schedules in line with program goals  
  
Assess supplier readiness to support build events and production ramp. Identify potential execution issues and provide recommendations to mitigate risk.  
  
You will utilize your Quality Engineering background in the following areas:  
  
Quality Planning  
  
Apply solid understanding of quality control and manufacturing concepts to develop specific Product Quality Plan (PQP) appropriate to program and commodity.  
  
Coordinate all Quality Engineering functions for a program, serving as project manager to lead efforts at supplier locations.  
  
Actively participate in the program planning and monitoring process assuming responsibility for key deliverables at all milestones.  
  
Provide technical direction and guidance to other Quality Engineers supporting the implementation of the PQP.  
  
Assess measurability and creatively address concerns directly with stakeholders. Identify and direct studies to implement improvements in measuring method where appropriate.  
  
Establish audit procedures appropriate to program and supplier to ensure adherence to Apple quality standards. Implement FAI and Cp/Cpk reviews of mechanical parts.

Assists supplier selection process for new products and second sourcing activities supporting qualification/disqualification decisions.  
  
Review PQP with supplier and other Apple functional groups to optimize supplier quality programs. Evaluates supplier readiness and adherence to PQP at all development and qualification stages.  
  
Monitor each supplier's performance through measurement of production line statistics, company inspections, and audits. Prepare summary of performance and communicate to appropriate management to ensure effective corrective action plans can be promptly executed.
